beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Some businesses never need to persuade customers that the problem exists.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The pain, the embarrassment, or the deadline has already done that work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Aspirin, Viagra, and Coffins asks what entrepreneurs should do with this uncomfortable advantage.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book places human suffering, research, and commercial opportunity at the same table.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its tone is ironic, but its central question is serious.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Does a business reduce vulnerability, or become more profitable by keeping it alive?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading it means looking at markets through the needs that polite pitch decks often hide.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The title introduces three market signals rather than a guide to those particular products.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Aspirin stands for a recognized problem whose relief the customer can notice.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Viagra marks intimate demand shaped by discretion, identity, and embarrassment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Coffins point to unavoidable need when customers have little time or bargaining strength.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These signals organize an argument about urgency, trust, and the terms of exchange.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They also expose why genuine value and exploitation can appear in the same market.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks readers to investigate that boundary instead of treating demand as an ethical endorsement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Before examining new markets, the book challenges a convenient story about the past.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Earlier communities could provide belonging while also imposing constraint, danger, and limited privacy.
